availability.note: Ford Australia MY26.5 Ranger Hybrid line-up: XL, Sport, Wildtrak, all 4x4 dual-cab pickups; XLT and limited-edition Stormtrak dropped (CarExpert, CarsGuide, 4X4 Australia agree on three grades). ford.com.au Build & Price returned 403, so the configurator could not be read. CarExpert spec listing https://www.carexpert.com.au/ford/ranger/2026-xl-2-3l-cab-chassis-4x4-electric-jskf8of520260731 shows the XL Hybrid as a 2026 model released 5 July 2026.

listPrice.note: Ford publishes only 'recommended driveaway' $59,000 (footnote: includes dealer delivery and statutory charges; private, fleet and government buyers; participating dealers; no state split, no end date). Ute divisor: (59000 - 880) / 1.027 = 56592; round-trip through calc/onroad.js driveAwayPrice (isNonPassenger true) = 58,999.98. Not independently verifiable: no outside on-road estimate exists. CarExpert's spec page says 'prices starting at $61,000 before on-road costs', which is $2,000 ABOVE Ford's own drive-away and would cost about $63,527 on the road in VIC, so it is an RRP that Ford's national drive-away undercuts (the same $2,000 gap on all three grades shows the drive-away is a flat national figure, not a VIC calculation); rejected in favour of the manufacturer's own price. Because the drive-away bundles dealer delivery, the back-out may overstate list by ~$1,500-2,000. Same $59,000/$66,000/$70,000 drive-away in CarExpert, CarsGuide and 4X4 Australia.

batteryKwh.note: Ford AU '11.8kWh usable'; Auto Express UK data gives 16.5 gross / 11.8 usable for the same pack.

rangeKm.note: Ford of Europe footnote 'pure electric driving range up to 43 km WLTP'. The Australian 49km claim (CarExpert spec page, called NEDC by CarExpert) is above the WLTP figure, so rejected per the direction test. Auto Express UK lists 42km WLTP EAER for a Wildtrak.

consumptionKwhPer100km.note: batteryKwh / rangeKm x 100 = 11.8 / 43 x 100 = 27.44; no published WLTP EV-mode figure (CarExpert quotes 18.7kWh/100km against the NEDC 49km, a different standard). Tautological against the cross-check.

combinedRangeKm.note: rangeKm + tank / fuelConsumptionL100km x 100 = 43 + 70 / 8.3 x 100 = 886. Tank 70L per CarExpert spec page https://www.carexpert.com.au/ford/ranger/2026-xl-2-3l-cab-chassis-4x4-electric-jskf8of520260731, Chasing Cars and the CarExpert review.

fuelConsumptionL100km.note: No published charge-sustaining figure. 4X4 Australia's overall on-test 8.3L/100km, mostly highway after the battery was depleted (Auto EV and EV Charge modes), on the unchanged 2.3/11.8kWh powertrain. Other evidence: 6.9 on a 60km hybrid loop (same review), 9.3 over a week with heavy hauling (CarsGuide XLT). Replaces the held 8.5, which had no recorded source. Close to siblings gwm-cannon-phev 8.1 and byd-shark-6 7.9.

isFuelEfficientForLct.note: Combined label 2.9 L/100km, at or below 3.5. Also CarExpert and CarsGuide news. Every row is under $80,809 anyway.

isGreenForVicDuty.note: Ute: field rules require false on every ute row; Victoria charges utes as goods vehicles (isNonPassengerForVicDuty true).

bootLitresSeatsUp.note: Ford publishes no tub litres. CarExpert MY26.5 spec page https://www.carexpert.com.au/ford/ranger/2026-xl-2-3l-cab-chassis-4x4-electric-jskf8of520260731: cargo length 1471mm (top), width 1584mm; depth 498mm per CarExpert's PHEV review and CarsGuide. 1471 x 1584 x 498 = 1160 L; ignores the 1233mm between-arch width so reads 10-20% high. CarsGuide's tray figures (1605 x 1523 x 498) give 1217 L. Replaces held 1185 (no recorded source). Siblings: Cannon 1196, Cannon Alpha 1140, Shark 6 1200.

towKg.note: 'Braked towing 3,500 kg' (750kg unbraked); Ford AU line-up release: max braked 3,500kg with genuine tow pack. 2,566kg kerb; 16-inch steel wheels on this listing (CarExpert news says 17-inch alloys).

warrantyYears.note: 60 months, unlimited km; battery 8 years/160,000km per CarExpert review. No servicing condition.

insuranceAnnual.note: Anchored to gwm-cannon-phev-lux (1700 at $48,793, itself anchored to this row) and byd-shark-6-premium (1800 at $57,900); kept at the held 1700 as the lowest-spec Ranger.

depreciationCurve.note: Held curve kept, below the mainstream default: Ford cut Ranger PHEV prices by about $10,000-13,000 within a year of launch (April 2026 campaign, then permanent MY26.5 repricing), which marks down early used values. Sits above the GWM ute curve and Ford's own Mach-E curves; no newer evidence found.
